newsitem.title: USA: Boomtown says weather hurts Reno casino. [CORRECTED 23:13 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Boomtown says weather hurts Reno casino. [CORRECTED 23:13 GMT]

text.p: Boomtown Inc, a hotel and casino operator, on Tuesday said fiscal first (corrects from fourth) quarter revenues at its casino in Reno were hurt by the recent foul weather that hit northern California and the Pacific Northwest.

In a statement, the company said earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA), which is a common measure of performance in the gambling industry, will be roughly $2.1 million below year ago levels.
The rain and snow storms caused rivers to flood and in some places closed Interstate 80, which on the weekends accounts for a majority of Boomtown Reno's customer volume.
At its three other casinos in Las Vegas, New Orleans and Biloxi, Miss., Boomtown said it expects "slight improvements" in earnings.
The company's fiscal first quarter ended December, 31. It expects to report earnings during the week of January 20. Boomtown currently is in the process of merging with Hollywood Park Inc.
